acceptance_criteria: The site where the timeout sets the unit status is quoted, with its file and line.
The runner's stop reason and the workflow terminal are separate fields, demonstrated.
A wall-clock deadline produces a workflow terminal naming the deadline, demonstrated by a test that simulates it.
The call ceiling and iteration bounds still produce their terminals — asserted.
A run that reached a real terminal is unaffected — asserted.
No loop bound, threshold, gate condition or verdict semantics changed.
Suite count reported before and after.
assumptions: The timeout is enforced by the eval runner or the graph executor and sets the unit status. If it is enforced outside both, say so — the fix may belong where the scenario default lives rather than in the executor.
constraints: RULED INSTRUMENT REPAIR (Ruling D23). It changes what the RECORD carries, not what any verdict, gate or loop concludes. Record the ruling before implementing it.

FIRST, LOCATE THE SITE, do not assume it: find where the unit record's status is set to 'blocked' on a timeout, and quote the code. Name the field and the line. If the runner's stop-reason and the workflow terminal share one field today, that is the defect and this command names it explicitly.

TWO SEPARATE FIELDS: the runner's stop reason (for example 'timed_out_after_600s') and the workflow's terminal status must never be the same field. A reader must be able to tell a workflow that concluded blocked from a runner that killed a workflow that never concluded.

EVERY BOUND PRODUCES A WORKFLOW TERMINAL NAMING IT. The deadline is the one B18 missed. When the wall-clock budget is reached, the run emits a terminal whose reason names the deadline in the operator's words, exactly as the call ceiling and iteration bounds now do.
Do NOT change any loop's max_iterations, any threshold, any gate condition, or any verdict semantics. Do NOT extend any bound.
Do NOT change what the runner does about a timeout — it still stops the run. Only the record changes: it now says both what the runner did and what the workflow's terminal is.

One test per bound, each simulating its own condition end to end (convention 22): the call ceiling, an exhausted iteration bound, and the wall-clock deadline. The deadline test must simulate the deadline being reached, not assert on a mocked return.
Prove the deadline test by breaking it: remove the terminal emission and show the assertion fail.
Confirm the pre-existing -053 work still holds: the exhausted terminal still names the unmet criteria. This change adds the deadline path and must not regress the others.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.
evidence: .orchestration/responses/ARCH-20260923-049.response.json — 'Unit record status: blocked with error timed out after 600s — that is the runner timeout label, not a workflow terminal'
HANDOVER.md §4.2 B18 (corrected to CLOSED IN PART by -065) — the call ceiling, spend ceiling and iteration bounds produce typed terminals; the deadline does not
.orchestration/responses/ARCH-20260922-043.response.json — the fold records an abstention distinctly; the same shape applied to a stop reason
workflows/engineering-rnd.yaml — review_rework_loop max_iterations review_rework_attempts, on_exhausted escalation; the loop bound was never reached because wall-clock ended the run first
AGENTS.md convention 26 — a reading mistakable for a stronger claim is a defect in the instrument
AGENTS.md convention 28 — an instrument asserts it computed its subject before it asserts anything about it
AGENTS.md convention 22 — an instrument's test simulates the condition it watches, end to end
objective: Make every bound produce a workflow terminal, including the wall-clock deadline, and separate the runner's stop-reason from the workflow's terminal status.

preconditions.command: grep -rn 'timed out after\|status.*blocked\|timeout' autornd/evals/*.py autornd/graph/executor.py | head -20
preconditions.expected: Locate the timeout site; record the file and line.
Locate the bounds that already emit terminals, as the pattern to follow.
Present. If absent, return BLOCKED naming ARCH-20260925-065.

questions: Should the workflow's own deadline be a scenario setting, a workflow setting, or a settings value? D25 says a scenario declares its budget; the loop must then observe it. Report which layer currently owns the 600s and which should.

If a loop's iterations can exceed the wall-clock budget even when the budget is generous, should the loop prefer its iteration bound or the deadline — which wins? My reading is the deadline, because it is the outer bound, but state what the code shows.
rollback: Revert the commit; the timeout returns to writing the runner's label into the workflow terminal's field.
transport: Commit this command file verbatim as carriage before executing; commit the response IN_PROGRESS first, then update it in place. delivery_state must carry the PR number per Ruling D16.

verification.command: .venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -k 'deadline or timeout or terminal or bound'
verification.expected: One test per bound, including the deadline.
The timeout label is distinguishable from a terminal status.
